raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: Hausman-Taylor panel regressions (2008-2019, normalized log municipal coverage rates): Urban water supply coverage (Table 6, Col. 2, PDF p. 20; N = 1,747 obs across 802 municipalities): earmarked SGP water/sanitation transfers Lnsgpagua beta = 1.188 (SE = 0.462, p < 0.05), municipal property tax Lnpredia beta = 0.429 (SE = 0.153, p < 0.01), municipal management index Lnmdm_ges beta = -7.253 (SE = 2.519, p < 0.01). Rural water supply coverage (Table 6, Col. 3, PDF p. 20; N = 1,948 obs across 860 municipalities): Lnsgpagua beta = -0.131 (SE = 0.423, ns), local tax revenue Lntribut beta = 0.433 (SE = 0.153, p < 0.01), royalties Lnregal beta = -0.0650 (SE = 0.0307, p < 0.05), Lnmdm_ges beta = 6.578 (SE = 2.130, p < 0.01). Urban sewerage coverage (Table 7, Col. 2, PDF p. 22; N = 1,848 obs across 823 municipalities): Lnsgpagua beta = 0.136 (SE = 0.367, ns), Lnpredia beta = 0.516 (SE = 0.140, p < 0.01), Lnmdm_ges beta = -6.079 (SE = 1.781, p < 0.01). Rural sewerage coverage (Table 7, Col. 3, PDF p. 22; N = 1,631 obs across 767 municipalities): voter turnout Lnturnout beta = -1.640 (SE = 0.800, p < 0.05), Lntribut beta = 0.426 (SE = 0.180, p < 0.05), Lnmdm_ges beta = 5.521 (SE = 1.886, p < 0.01).
raw_response.publication_year_note: Published in Apuntes del CENES, Volumen 45, Número 81, Enero - Junio 2026, pp. 147-176 (received 16 January 2025; approved 6 August 2025; no separate online-first publication year printed).
raw_response.rationale: Full text (30 pages, Spanish) is complete and accessible. Using a 3-period municipal panel (2008-2019; up to 893 Colombian municipalities) and Hausman-Taylor instrumental-variable panel estimators (Tables 6 and 7, PDF pp. 20 and 22), the study reports inferential regression coefficients with standard errors and p-value thresholds testing fiscal, administrative, and political decentralization mechanisms—specifically statutory earmarked intergovernmental water/sanitation transfers under Law 1176 of 2007 (Lnsgpagua), local own-source property and tax revenues (Lnpredia, Lntribut), municipal administrative management capacity (Lnmdm_ges), Functional Urban Area governance/spatial status (Dummy AUF), and electoral turnout (Lnturnout)—on residential urban and rural drinking water and sewerage coverage rates (Criterion 4). These institutional-capacity, fiscal-decentralization, and administrative-structure exposures fit SWiM Family C (with secondary links to Family B for earmarked intergovernmental transfers/turnout and Family A for decentralized municipal governance arrangements).
